newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa tumbles to lower close as specs sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa tumbles to lower close as specs sell.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures slumped to their lowest levels in 10 days on Wednesday, hit by heavy speculative liquidation in a sharp correction to the market's recent bull run.
Benchmark September futures tumbled $71 per tonne, to end at $1,614, the lowest close since June 20.
Traders said a growing consensus that the market's dazzling climb to nine-year highs in June had been overdone sent prices spiralling downward this morning.
Technically, the September contract's failure on Tuesday to clear a contract high set just last week of $1,737 prompted speculators to liquidate long positions early on.
Manufacturer-linked buying briefly stemmed the slide, but the funds later resumed their onslaught, dragging September to an intraday low of $1,610.
Cocoa prices have lost more than five percent of their value in the past two days.
While news related to next season's harvest in West Africa has been scarce in recent days, analysts said signs of more favorable growing weather in the Ivory Coast have cast a shadow over the market.
"A lot of this is linked to the belief that the Ivory Coast's (1997/98) main crop is not really encountering any defined problems," said Steve Platt, senior analyst with Dean Witter in Chicago.

"It seemed like the market really did not have a lot of justification for being at those high levels," he said. "The market has been overbought...and the failure against (resistance) levels led to the rather accelerated liquidation pressure today."
Traders said September would need to hold above the $1,580 level to ward off another round of fund liquidation.
"There is no panic yet, but any further falls could bring in some panic selling," a trader said.
If $1,580 were breached, a subsequent objective awaited at $1,550. To the upside, stiff resistance was noted toward the $1,680-1,700 range.
The day's volume was estimated at 13,515 lots.
